title: Cabbage Rolls with Rice and Herbs
subtitle: slow-baked with prunes, pomegranate and walnuts
description: Cabbage leaves stuffed with a round rice, walnut and herb filling and baked slowly with prunes, mint, silan and pomegranate molasses until the rice is soft and the sauce sweet and tangy.

steps.text: Remove the core of the white cabbage with a small knife and place the cabbage in a pot with enough boiling water to cover. Cook for about 10-15 minutes until the leaves come away easily. Remove the cabbage but keep the water. Cool and gently separate the leaves, removing any hard central ribs.
In the reserved cooking water, cook the red cabbage and prunes for about 10 minutes until the water is coloured and the cabbage has softened a little. Remove with a slotted spoon and keep the water.
Make the filling: place the rice in a bowl, add the remaining filling ingredients and mix carefully so as not to break the rice.

Place a cabbage leaf concave side up. Put a heaped spoonful of filling in the centre and fold from the base outwards. Fold in the left and right edges and finish rolling, taking care not to roll too tightly. Arrange the rolls in an ovenproof pot, seam side down.

Scatter the prunes and mint leaves over the rolls. Season with salt and pepper and drizzle with silan, pomegranate molasses and oil. Pour in enough of the reserved cooking water to reach the top of the rolls and cover with red cabbage leaves. Cover with foil.

Bake for 1 hour, reduce the temperature to 100°C and bake for another 2 hours. Raise the temperature back to 200°C, remove the cover and the red cabbage leaves and bake for about 10 minutes until browned.
Serve hot with a vegetable salad on the side.
